summary: The pinned bundle and frozen sandbox evidence match the requested task and candidate, and the recorded C unit test passed. The candidate has a protocol behavior regression: several newly recognized business commands are treated as successful after returning a position response, without executing those commands. Recovery coverage is also incomplete.
findings: The bundle SHA256 matches the supplied value. The pinned candidate, checkout log, patch hash, and server evidence are consistent; the recorded GCC test exited 0 and passed all six suites.

In minimc_proto.c, the new handlers for SET_TEMP, motion, filament/slot, and job commands return true after sending a temperature or position response. They only update debug bookkeeping and do not perform the requested business operation. This also bypasses the previous unknown-command NACK fallback, so callers can receive a success-shaped response for an operation that was not performed. The unit tests assert debug text but do not verify the response semantics or command execution.

Negative-case coverage does not verify the contract’s recovery behavior: after a full debug ring is drained, the test does not confirm a new log is accepted; after simulated USART2 TX failure, it resets busy state but does not send a subsequent frame and assert ACK; after relay timeout, it does not verify a successful subsequent cascade send/response.

The only recorded compile/test command excludes main.c, although the candidate substantially refactors startup and the main loop to integrate debug draining. No full firmware build or main-loop integration evidence is present. The source report field is empty, so no report or report SHA256 was available to audit.
accepted_scope: Software sandbox and C unit-test review for the pinned TWIN-44 candidate: USART2 921600 reconfiguration, debug ring behavior, structured logging, TX failure suppression, CRC and relay timeout handling. Physical MCU HIL is explicitly outside this task’s acceptance scope.
unexecuted: Physical MCU firmware flashing and hardware-in-the-loop verification.
Full firmware build and integration verification of the main.c startup/loop changes.
Explicit recovery checks for ring-buffer drain, successful send after busy recovery, and successful cascade forwarding after relay timeout.
Protocol-level validation that newly recognized business commands execute their intended operation and produce correct wire responses.
